subject: Geofence routing and deletion SLA — technical confirmations for Dedicated

Subject: Dedicated deployment — routing to US-only and deletion confirmation

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo this week. Two quick items we need to confirm before procurement can move forward: 1) for our Dedicated deployment, can you guarantee that inference traffic and all customer-derived artifacts (requests, logs, KV caches) will remain in the US region we select (no cross-region mirroring or backups), and 2) what does your deletion process look like when we request erasure of a dataset/tenant (timeline, proof of deletion, and whether snapshots/backups are purged)?

We have an internal control that requires geofenced data residency and a documented deletion SLA. If you can provide a short technical note or runbook pointer, that would be ideal.

Also looping in security@acmehealth.com for any compliance questions.

—Tom
Tom Gray
Head of InfoSec, Acme Health

Tom — thanks for the clear questions. Happy to confirm at a high level and then Marcus/Neha can add the technical specifics. Quick summary up front: yes — Dedicated can be provisioned with a US-only VPC and data plane; we support strict routing policies so requests, artifacts, and KV caches stay in that region. For deletion, we have a documented erasure workflow that targets primary storage, KV caches, and backups; typical SLA is 30 days end-to-end with attestations available on request.

Marcus — can you attach the deployment diagram and the deletion runbook excerpt for Tom? Neha — can you confirm whether we support forced snapshot purge and the exact timeline if the customer requests immediate escrow-level deletion?

Tom — I attached a short diagram and our deletion runbook excerpt for context (see attachments). If you prefer, we can set a 30‑minute call for the security team to walk through the flow.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment — routing to US-only and deletion confirmation

Tom / Vanessa — attaching the redwood-dedicated-dataflow-diagram.pdf (exported from our internal infra docs). Key points: 

- Region selection: When a Dedicated pool is provisioned we pin the compute and storage resources to the selected cloud region (US-West-2 in your case). The control plane (managed by Redwood) is logically separate; we offer a private control plane option for enterprise customers that want the control plane in their VPC.
- Network isolation: Dedicated pools run in customer-specific subnets with security groups and ACLs that prevent outbound cross-region replication. Backups are configurable — by default we keep snapshots in the same region; cross-region backups are opt-in and require customer approval.
- Logging & telemetry: Audit logs and traces can be routed to the customer's logging endpoint in the region. We can also deliver logs via S3 bucket in the same region or push to your SIEM via private peering.

Deletion specifics (high level):
- Primary data deletion: deletion command triggers background job to delete primary blobs and metadata; typical completion: 24–72 hours depending on data size.
- Cache/KV: KV caches and ephemeral runtime caches are invalidated immediately; persistent KV entries are scheduled for purge and removed within 72 hours.
- Snapshots/backups: by default snapshots are retained for 30 days; we can configure immediate snapshot purge on contract (requires coordination with ops; subject to replication delays up to 7 days if snapshot is mid-write).
- Proof: we provide a signed attestation (PDF) that lists resources deleted and timestamps; for Dedicated we can provide deeper audit artifacts on request (hashes, object names).

I've included the diagram and the deletion-runbook-v1.2.md excerpt. If you need stronger guarantees (shorter retention/instant snapshot destruction), we can propose a contractual addendum and an ops play to enforce forced snapshot purge within 48 hours post-request.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — that helps. A couple follow-ups from our compliance team: 1) we need the deletion attestation to include S3 object keys (or equivalent storage identifiers) and a timestamped signature; 2) the 30‑day snapshot retention is okay by default but we need an option to trigger immediate snapshot purge with a defined escalation path (ops oncall + ticket + 48-hour SLA). Can you confirm you will accept a contract clause for forced snapshot purge and provide the attestation format sample? Also, please confirm whether any monitoring/analytics data that Redwood collects for billing/observability (token counts, latency metrics) is exported or stored outside the selected region.

We can do a short call later today if needed.

—Tom

Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment — routing to US-only and deletion confirmation

Tom — quick answers in line: 

- Attestation contents: we will provide a signed PDF attestation that includes the storage identifiers (S3 object keys or internal blob IDs), deletion timestamps (UTC), deleting operator ID, and a SHA256 digest of the deleted object list. We'll attach a sample attestation to the contract package.
- Forced snapshot purge: we confirm we will accept a contract clause for forced snapshot purge. Operationally, invoking the clause triggers: 1) high-priority ticket to Redwood Ops, 2) oncall escalation (+30m), 3) snapshot purge workflow (target: complete within 48 hours). We'll include the exact workflow and escalation contacts in the contract addendum.
- Monitoring/analytics: billing tokens and aggregated latency metrics are stored in the same region for Dedicated by default. The control plane aggregates some anonymized usage stats for platform health; if you select the private control plane option we can ensure control-plane telemetry does not leave your VPC. We will not export customer request payloads out of the pinned region.

Attachments: acme-dedicated-terms-redlines-20260115.pdf (our proposed redlines including the snapshot purge clause), sample_attestation_example.pdf (demo attestation).

Please let us know if you want a joint call to walk the redlines — Vanessa, can you propose a 30m slot today or Monday?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
